title: Make HTML 5.4 or 5.5 exclusive to 64-bit x86 and ARM processors, once either gets announced.
body:
In the years after XHTML 2.0 was cancelled and even a few years after Adobe Flash was discontinued, many major modern web browsers  are getting bloated and resource intensive to the point that 32-bit processors are now struggling to run these web browsers, and many modern HTML5 websites now struggle to run on older Windows XP through Windows 7-era hardware due to new advancements in web browser technology. In addition 32-bit x86 and ARM processors of the 2000s and early to mid-2010s have lost full developer support to which newer security issues are now being introduced in the years after those processors were discontinued, and have no home for modern web standards anymore.

In any new announcement in a couple of years for if HTML 5.4 and HTML 5.5 ever get announced in the future by either the W3C or WHATWG, HTML 5.5 would likely be exclusive to 64-bit and HTML 5.4 would likely be the final version of HTML for 32-bit processors.

A couple of options for both the WHATWG and W3C have are as follows:

- Make HTML 5.4 the final version for 32-bit x86 and ARM processors.
- Make HTML 5.5 exclusive to 64-bit x86 and ARM processors.
- Delist all 32-bit versions of HTML after HTML 5.4 is retired.
- Make all software and web browser developers only utilize the 64-bit exclusive HTML 5.5.

Again, as I said at the beginning, many major modern web browsers  are getting bloated and resource intensive to the point that 32-bit processors are now struggling to run these web browsers natively.

Hopefully the W3C and WHATWG announces either HTML 5.4 or HTML 5.5 anytime soon.
